items.item_text: Graduation with BS degree with specialization in biology, botany, zoology, geography or comparable field and one year experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
M.S. degree in biology, botany, zoology, geography or comparable field.
Is exposed to marked changes in temperature and/or humidity: Yes
Drives motorized equipment: Yes
Dust: Yes
Other: Exposure to smoke during wildfire season (several months during year). Erratic weather that includes heavy snow for multiple weeks in October through May. Occasional heavy flooding.
Computer experience with word processor, spreadsheet and database operating systems and commonly used office applications (e.g., Word, Excel, Filemaker Pro, PowerPoint, Internet, email).
Basic understanding and experience in trail construction and maintenance
Computer knowledge and experience to develop and manage Reserve website
Previous experience in personnel management
Previous budgetary analysis experience
Experience operating heavy equipment (e.g. snow plow, chain saw, tractor)

Reserve Support and Management Assist the Reserve Director as needed with visitors for research, teaching and outreach activities, as well as administrative duties, including the preparation of the annual report. Manage visitor paperwork including sign-in sheets, billing invoices, application forms, and correspondence as needed. Assist Reserve director in facilitating visitor arrival/departure, including scheduling lodging/laboratory use, communicating Reserve rules and regulations, conducting check-out inspections, janitorial work and invoicing. Keep records of materials used, tasks performed. Support researchers and class with equipment needs as needed (e.g. audio visual projectors, field equipment). Select and purchase supplies and equipment, perform accounting tasks as needed and maintain all files and records. Assume responsibility for additional tasks assigned or delegated by the Reserve Director. Operate the Reserve in the absence of the Reserve Director. • Supervise people that come to reserve and monitor for safety. • Engage with visitors to provide orientation /safety information, and answer questions. Be available in a visible space for them to come talk to if needed. • Be alert and aware of people entering and exiting, as well as if they have an issue with entering reserve (check email, text messages, security cameras) • Send invoices • Regular email correspondence • Word processing including re-formatting and creating new documents. • Submit receipts with documentation in a timely manner. • Perform tasks like resetting wifi, security camera, checking that gate is locked. Be able to troubleshoot if things are not working. • Do some prep for groups like janitorial tasks (replace trash can liners, clean, take out trash, tidy up areas). • Reach out to on-campus groups to comply with fire safety regulations, chemical inventories. (50% time)

Facilities and Grounds Management Responsible for monitoring and maintaining a safe and functional facility including all buildings, surrounding grounds, and access roads. Investigate and lead ongoing improvement projects for the Reserve, taking ownership for results and keeping other team members informed of progress. Liaise with UCR Environmental Health & Safety and with UCR Campus Administration (EMN). Coordinate with contractors and vendors and supervise and work with various contractors. Maintain and upgrade instrumentation including internet connection, weather stations, solar power systems, and water systems. Patrol and mend fence lines, roads, and trails as needed. Safely clear impassable access roads during snow events using a bobcat/skidsteer. Monitor and manage maintenance of well, plumbing and septic systems, including creating quarterly reports. Maintain and improve facilities (7 buildings), including staff office equipment: computer, printer, internet communications. Monitor and follow up for essential care of all vehicles. Conduct inventory and inspection of fire and safety equipment and supplies. Work closely with roving UCNRS steward when necessary. • Spearhead facilities improvement projects • Help address pest issues as they arise, including monitoring for any signs of new pest infestations (mice, bats, ants) and implementing corrective actions. • Drive to purchase supplies such as toilet paper, or hardware from hardware store. • Take inventories and keep track of supplies. Record propane levels and monitor. • Help roving steward with tasks like trail maintenance. • Troubleshoot daily operations like a clogged toilet or resetting internet connection • Anticipate needs based on weather conditions (ex. draining water lines if freezing overnight temps expected, turning off heaters when not needed) • Turn off valves in case of emergency (ex. water line breaks) • Help plow snow if needed during winter using bobcat/skidsteer (30% time)

Database and Other Information Management: Maintain and manage database files for museum collections, environmental monitoring and research programs. Develop and maintain GPS and GIS mapping and databases. Update website and website databases. Conduct literature reviews; update Reserve publications lists and regional bibliographies. Manage and enhance monitoring flora and fauna at the James and Oasis de los Osos Reserves and supporting databases, species lists, phenology records, on-site transects and meteorological data. Supervise contractors, volunteers, or seasonal restoration/resource management crews. (10% time)

Research and Education Support Under the direction of the Reserve Director: assist in organizing, teaching or attending workshops, meetings and conferences. Develop displays, presentations, and publications (e.g., brochures, guides); provide technical assistance and comments to government agencies as requested. Prepare and present programs on aspects of natural history and reserve site activities to classes and other visitors. Participate in public outreach activities including teaching, guided tours and lectures/demonstrations. Collaborate with federal and state agencies and other institutions on regional research, education and environmental management issues. (10% time)
Required to hold valid driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program.
Read/Comprehend: Frequently

Perform Calculations: Occasionally
Communicate Orally: Frequently
Reason & Analyze: Frequently

Other: James Reserve has multiple steep inclines that must be traversed frequently throughout the day. Must be able to shovel snow and rake grounds for fire abatement. Must be able to load material in truck and bring to disposal site.

Basic understanding of state and federal agencies and regulatory policies that apply to research and land management issues. Ability to learn names of plants, animals, geological formations, places and basic natural history of area surrounding the reserves. Knowledge of management of museum data collections.
Demonstrated abilities in writing for basic science and general subjects (e .g., articles , letters , brochures).
Must be able to work independently with little direction. Ability to guide volunteers and others in reserve work.
General knowledge of, or willingness to learn, alternative technologies (e.g. solar power)

Ability to perform work outside, under adverse weather conditions. Knowledge of basic maintenance techniques for electrical, plumbing, fencing, roads and physical plant, or willingness to learn. Able to stay overnight at reserve site when necessary. Must be able to operate and/or willing to operate all kinds of equipment needed to perform duties.
General knowledge of, or willingness to learn, network connectivity for Starlink and wifi
Must have a valid driver's license, and must be able to drive a bobcat tractor or be willing to learn.
Skills in interpersonal communication and oral presentation.
Must have the capacity to operate and work with heavy equipment. This includes 4WD vehicles, chain saw, and others as necessary
